learningObjective: Trace how corpus-wide pair counts create ranked, reusable BPE tokens that compress common words while leaving rarer words as multiple pieces.
mediumRationale: A vertical semantic trace is the smallest medium that keeps each corpus segmentation beside the pair count and vocabulary addition it causes. Four labelled panels expose the otherwise hidden loop: merge the most frequent current pair everywhere, recount, retain the learned rank, and replay those ranked merges on new text.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a flowchart can repeat count and merge stages, but automatic node layout would not preserve the exact token segmentation and arithmetic within each round as clearly as ordered text panels.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: deterministic geometry could align token chips, but the lesson is a discrete sequence of corpus states rather than a geometric relationship. SVG would add markup and make text wrapping at phone width less robust.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: semantic headings, code fragments, explicit arithmetic, and logical source order make every merge inspectable, stack naturally at 390 CSS pixels, and remain useful without color or client-side code.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: changing frequencies or stepping through merges would add controls and state when one carefully chosen three-round trace is enough to reveal the counting and rank-order invariants.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the 2016 ACL paper is available under CC BY 4.0 and could be adapted with attribution, while the Hugging Face course documentation is Apache 2.0 and tiktoken is MIT licensed. Their figures, examples, code, wording, data, and layouts were not reused. The shipped map/maps/cap corpus, counts, structure, and application examples are independently authored.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose lists the BPE loop but requires readers to mentally update a corpus after every merge, aggregate a pair across word frequencies, and connect learned merge rank to later segmentation. The trace makes those state transitions explicit.

pages.insight: The preceding slide implements a character-level LSTM language model. It establishes the character baseline that subword tokenization improves on, but provides no tokenizer mechanism or reusable visual.

The only dedicated tokenization slide defines subword fragments and lists an iterative BPE procedure beside perplexity. It provides no worked merge state. Its statement that WordPiece repeatedly merges the most frequent pair is too loose, so that wording was not carried into the visual.
The following slide moves to text representation learning and contrasts autoregressive, masked-language-model, and multitask objectives. It does not explain token construction.
A later RoBERTa slide mentions its larger GPT-2 byte-level BPE vocabulary, supporting model-family context but adding no algorithm trace.
A later OLMo slide records a modified GPT-NeoX BPE tokenizer and vocabulary padding to a multiple of 128. This is implementation context, not an explanation of merge learning.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that BPE does not independently chunk each word into intuitive morphemes. It learns a global ranked merge list by repeatedly counting adjacent symbols in the current corpus segmentation. In the original toy byte-level corpus, map occurs five times, maps three times, and cap twice. The pair a+p therefore occurs 10 times and becomes ap; m+ap then occurs eight times and becomes map; map+s occurs three times and becomes maps. Replaying those ranks yields [maps], [c][ap], and [t][r][ap][s]. Counts and segmentations were recalculated manually and are explanatory rather than empirical tokenizer claims.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed the full 214-page deck, rendered and inspected physical pages 97-99, reviewed incidental matches on pages 102 and 107, and cross-checked the merge mechanism against the primary NLP paper and official tokenizer documentation with explicit license treatment.

implementation.accessibility: The figure has a linked learning-question title and a role=list child with a complete accessible label. Every panel states its round, current segmentation, exact pair arithmetic, and resulting vocabulary token in text; learned order and output boundaries use headings, rank numbers, brackets, and code typography rather than color. The established one-column responsive grid has no minimum width and wraps at 390 CSS pixels. Shared theme variables supply dark-mode contrast, while established print rules force a light high-contrast palette and avoid splitting the figure.
